_why: parse_query dispatches on the first token and returns the sub-parser's result without checking the input was consumed. A sub-parser that reads a valid PREFIX returns Ok and the remainder is silently discarded. Three independent reproducers, all this root cause: #1895's WITHIN GROUP, the bare-alias counter-example, and a statement-merge found by #1929's gate.

anchors._note: the defect: dispatch, return, no EOF check
the ONLY call site — the single insertion point for the fix
TokenType::Eof already exists; the check needs no new token

blast_radius._note: 54 refs across src/ tests/ examples/ (was 45 when first specced). Most are CALLERS of parse_query, and that is the point: every one of them currently accepts a valid prefix. The change is ~30 lines in mod.rs; the WORK is the fallout across those call sites and the SQL corpus.

acceptance: parse_query returns Err when the input is not fully consumed, naming the first unconsumed token and its position
a trailing statement terminator (`;`) is still tolerated — some callers pass SQL with it intact
the three named fail_to_pass tests exist, and each was verified to FAIL before the production change

every pre-existing test and shipped .sql file that now fails is TRIAGED, not silenced: each is either a genuine defect the check surfaced (fix the SQL, cite it) or a legitimate construct the parser should support (fix the parser, cite it)
forbidden: do not weaken or narrow the EOF check to make a failing test pass — a test that now fails is the check working; triage it
do not delete, #[ignore] or narrow any existing test
do not assume the existing STEP 1 commit on this branch is correct — evaluate it
do not create a branch: the worktree is already on the branch velo-dispatch cut for you
stop_conditions: more than ~15 pre-existing tests fail — STOP and report the list; that is a corpus-wide decision, not a fix to grind through
a shipped demo/*.sql or docs example turns out to rely on prefix-truncation — STOP and report which, before changing it
the fix appears to need changes inside individual sub-parsers rather than the one call site — STOP, that is a wider structural change than this spec pins
you cannot make a named fail_to_pass test fail before the change — report it rather than writing a vacuous test
